coverageNotes: Tests the separate transaction boundary of scheduled continuation batches. Does not prove arbitrary payloads fit a fixed batch size, liveness under continuous writes, or production job recovery.

questions.concept: Scheduled mutations have a separate transaction boundary
questions.question: After the scheduled mutation fails, what does the original client call return and how many rows remain?

options.text: The original call fails with "Continuation failed"; all 205 rows remain.
options.rationale: Awaiting runAfter awaits scheduling, not execution of the scheduled mutation. The later error is not the original client result.

options.text: The original call returns null; 5 rows remain because both batches committed their deletes.
options.rationale: The failed scheduled mutation rolls back its own 100 attempted deletes.

options.text: The original call returns null; 205 rows remain because the continuation rolls back the whole job.
options.rationale: The scheduled mutation does not share the already committed parent transaction.

options.text: The original call returns null; 105 rows remain because only the first batch committed.
options.rationale: The initial 100 deletes commit with scheduling. The later transaction fails and preserves its 100 attempted deletions, leaving 105 rows.
